title: Matt LaFleur on the resilience of the team: ‘They’re going to keep battling and that’s all you can ask for’
headline: Josh Jacobs has surgery Friday with the long-term outlook unknown, so watch Chris Brooks' role. Lukas Van Ness missed Wednesday practice, and Skyy Moore may return for Week 10 at Minnesota.
summary: LaFleur spoke ahead of the Week 10 game against the Vikings. He called the Minnesota defense a constant problem for offenses because it puts them behind the sticks, creates lots of third-and-longs and forces mistakes, so Green Bay needs a clean game. He said Week 1 is mostly irrelevant, since the Vikings have changed a lot and Green Bay struggled to get everyone on the same page offensively in that loud building. He expects the pressure to be on his defense to communicate against a Vikings team with a new quarterback and likely new wrinkles. On injuries, Lukas Van Ness was one of several players who did not practice Wednesday and the coach called that a concern, though he may be out there Thursday. Skyy Moore may be back, which would boost the return game and possibly add a role on offense. Josh Jacobs has not had his surgery yet but is expected to tomorrow, and the long-term outlook will not be known until afterward. The coach stressed that the running game matters more as the weather turns and praised Chris Brooks' runs from the first meeting. He also praised Karl Brooks' consistency inside and called Jordan Love poised, resilient and playing as well as anybody in the league.

Coach said 'if he's able to go' he would boost the return game and could be used on offense, so his availability is not confirmed.
Surgery had not happened yet and was expected the next day; the long-term outlook will be clearer afterward.

signals.note: A pending surgery puts the lead back's availability in doubt, so manage the risk and line up a replacement.

signals.note: If Jacobs is out, Brooks is a possible beneficiary, though the coach did not commit to anything.

He downplayed the Week 1 loss. The loud environment caused offensive communication problems, and he expects pressure on his defense to stay on the same page against a Vikings team with a new quarterback and new wrinkles.
He stressed that running the ball matters more later in the season as the weather turns, especially at home.
He said the team has a one-play mindset and never feels out of the fight.

title: Sean McVay & Matthew Stafford discuss the trade deadline, injury timelines, Week 10 vs. the Cardinals & more
headline: Puka Nacua is out for an extended stretch (not going on IR), Terrance Ferguson is out a couple more weeks, and Davante Adams is realistically back after the Green Bay game. McDuffie is optimistic to play this week.
summary: McVay opened with the Wednesday DNP list: Steve Avila (hamstring), Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Trent McDuffie (back), Kamren Curl (toe) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring). Nacua will miss an extended period but won't go on IR, which McVay said is for roster-mechanics reasons. The Rams re-signed Xavier Smith and placed Jordan Whittington on IR with a back issue. They were quiet at the trade deadline because they expect injured players back soon and didn't want to fill voids as if they were season-long. Davante Adams is looking at a return after the Green Bay game. Ferguson is at least a couple of weeks away, and the Rams want to save him a roster spot before his 21-day clock runs out around Green Bay. McVay called having both running backs very valuable and said leaning on the run game matters regardless of health. He stressed flexibility in game plans, with new players getting chances in normal down-and-distance packages. The Rams face Arizona in Week 10 on a three-game win streak, and McDuffie is hoped to return this week.

topics.detail: The Rams explored moves but little materialized. McVay said it takes two sides to trade, and the team preferred waiting for injured players like Adams and Ferguson to return rather than filling voids for the whole season. Roster mechanics (48, 53, practice squad) were unusually complicated.

McVay said they will explore everything to maximize the available players, including personnel groupings, with a focus on normal downs and distances this week. He sees it as an opportunity for newer players to prove themselves. Stafford said they have used 13, 12 and 11 personnel this year and he is comfortable with whatever works.

Stafford said he trusts the receivers who will play and will throw to them in the game. He praised CJ Daniels, who has shown up in crossover practice tape and could get a chance on Sunday. Daniels is not on the provided roster.

McVay called the defense great lately and said the Rams will do whatever is necessary on offense. Stafford said Arizona's defense under a coordinator the Rams have faced often will present challenges.

McVay said Aaron has been having fun and playing great, sharing a moment with Myles after a sack. He said the team is proud of the three-game win streak but not complacent. They are looking to improve after a frustrating earlier loss to Arizona that he attributed to execution and energy.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Daiyan Henley Trade Situation and Facing the Ravens
headline: LB Daiyan Henley is back with the Chargers after the Broncos trade fell through over a medical-grade dispute; his practice status is TBD this week ahead of Monday night vs. the Ravens.
summary: Harbaugh said the Broncos made the Henley trade conditional on a medical pass/fail grade and tried to renegotiate for less compensation after the deadline. The Chargers refused, so the deal fell apart. He called this a loophole the league should examine. Henley flew back late Tuesday night, attended meetings and a walkthrough this morning, and was welcomed back warmly by the coaches and players. His practice participation and injury-report status are "TBD", though Harbaugh said they fully expect him to be available. Harbaugh declined to confirm reports of knee arthritis. On the Week 10 matchup, he praised Ravens coach Jesse Minter as a friend and a good head coach. He also praised Baltimore's multiple-front, coverage-disguising defense and called Derrick Henry's skills elite. He said red zone and third-down efficiency are an emphasis, and that the team's only goal is to win Monday night and build momentum. He expects Jacoby Brissett to start for Baltimore and was non-specific about the plan.

injuries.detail: Returned late Tuesday night after the failed trade; practice participation and injury-report designation are "TBD", though Harbaugh fully expects him to be available. He was on last week's injury report with a reported shoulder/knee issue, and Harbaugh wouldn't confirm a reported knee arthritis finding.

signals.claim: Henley is back with the team and is expected to be available and in the defensive rotation after meetings and a walkthrough.
signals.note: Henley stays in the Chargers' defense, which matters for IDP and the LA defensive outlook, though his practice status is uncertain.
signals.quote: we fully expect, uh, that he is.

signals.note: Harbaugh would not detail the knee/shoulder issue, so watch the practice reports for limited vs. full.
signals.quote: TBD on what will be on the personal guy got in late last night.

topics.detail: Harbaugh said Denver conditioned the trade on a medical pass/fail grade and wanted a lower pick than the agreed fourth- and fifth-round compensation. He called it a loophole that sets a bad precedent and said the league should look into it.
Baltimore uses multiple personnel groups, can stop both the run and the pass, and changes coverages, linebacker patterns and stunts, making the scheme look complex while executing it with ease.
Harbaugh called Henry's strength, speed, vision, patience and physicality elite and said that makes him hard to stop.
Harbaugh said red-zone scoring and extending drives on third down are emphasized, and that there were encouraging things from the offense at the end of the last game.
The team's stated focus is to win Monday night and get on a roll.

title: WATCH: Mike McCarthy Media Availability (Nov. 12)
headline: DT Derrick Harmon appears to be back at practice and on his planned workload, and Pittsburgh's veteran-managed defensive line rotation continues ahead of the Week 10 trip to Cincinnati.
summary: McCarthy spent most of the session on the Bengals, praising Joe Burrow and the passing game as a high-level operation with explosive plays, double moves and efficient execution. He called the AFC North the best football there is and framed the prime-time trip to Cincinnati as the kind of game you look forward to. He said the focus is on small details like turf, weather and night conditions, and on playing Pittsburgh's own style. On a player he called "Derek", who is almost certainly Derrick Harmon, he said the player hit the practice number the staff wanted the day before and that Wednesday's practice is a big one for everyone, since the team hasn't been in football function since the Cleveland game. He defended the defensive front rotation as a deliberate plan: veterans aren't worn down on Wednesdays and Thursdays, and young players get more reps. He added that the team is healthy enough that he isn't sure who his 48th active player is on Thursday. He said confidence is high after a couple of straight wins, and that handling success is the next challenge. He also downplayed red-zone rankings this early in the season. Finally, he praised rookie offensive lineman Max Iheanachor (captioned as "Max Hillman") for his work ethic and consistency, said he earned a 53-man roster spot before getting hurt, and said he's looking forward to getting him back.

injuries.detail: Coach said he hit the practice number the staff wanted for him the day before and is 'going okay' today. No setback was mentioned, but the transcript only says 'Derek', so the identification is inferred.
Rookie OL who got hurt earlier. Coach said it will be great to get him back into the fold, but gave no timeline or status.

signals.claim: Harmon is back at practice and working toward a normal role in the defensive front rotation against Cincinnati.
signals.note: He is trending toward full availability for the Bengals game, but the rotation plan means snaps may be managed.
signals.quote: he hit the number that they were looking to hit with him

signals.claim: Iheanachor is expected to return from injury and rejoin the roster, though no date was given.
signals.note: Coach praised him highly, but he is a depth lineman with no stated return date and little immediate fantasy impact.
signals.quote: he truly performed to a level that he deserved a 53 man roster spot

topics.detail: McCarthy called Cincinnati's offense elite. He credited Burrow's decision-making, pump fakes and double moves, and the way they move their receivers around. He said it is a challenge Pittsburgh is looking forward to.

The staff deliberately limits veterans' Wednesday and Thursday reps, working with the strength and medical staff. That gives young players more snaps and makes the roster deeper. He also said the roster is healthy enough that the 48th active player is still undecided.

Confidence is high after a couple of straight wins, and McCarthy's stated challenge is handling success. He said the team needs a strong Wednesday practice after not being in football function since the Cleveland game.

He said red-zone rankings don't matter until about four weeks into a season. He stressed the little things for the prime-time road game (turf, night conditions, weather) and playing on Pittsburgh's own terms.
